raw_response:
I'm 60 this year, been farming these 7 mu in Quzhou since I was 15. My wife and I manage it alone — our children work in Shijiazhuang and send a little money home, but not enough to live on. We have to watch every yuan.

This year I'm keeping 4 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, same as always. That's our main income and food security. The other land is 2 mu cotton and about 0.5 mu each of mungbean and red bean in small plots near the house. The beans are mostly for our own eating, but if the market price is decent we'll sell some at the village collection point.

For wheat, I plant around October 12th. I use an improved variety — I saved seed for two years but there was some disease last spring, so I'm buying fresh this year, about 25 yuan per mu. The extension agent told me 15 kg nitrogen per mu is the recommendation, but I tried 14 kg in 2019 and my wheat turned yellow by jointing. I ended up with only 380 kg/mu that year. Never again. I'm using 16 kg N per mu — about 10 kg equivalent as compound fertilizer at planting, then another 6 kg urea at jointing. Phosphorus about 6 kg, potassium about 4 kg. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing in March, and once at grain filling in late May. Pumping costs 30–40 yuan each time, but without it the yield drops badly. I spray herbicide in early spring, and if I see leaf rust I'll use fungicide. I hire a combine for harvest — costs about 50 yuan per mu — my wife and I can't cut 4 mu by hand anymore. Last year I got 450 kg/mu; this year I'm expecting about 460 if the weather cooperates.

Maize goes in immediately after wheat, June 12th to 15th. That window is terribly tight. After the combine finishes, I either rotary till quickly or sometimes plant no-till if the straw is too heavy to clear. I buy hybrid seed every year — can't save it, everyone knows hybrid doesn't breed true — costs about 40 yuan per mu. Fertilizer: compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at big flare stage, total about 15 kg N per mu, plus 5 kg P and 3 kg K. I irrigate twice in summer if there's no rain, sometimes only once in a wet July. One herbicide spray at planting. I expect about 480 kg/mu.

Cotton is on 2 mu, planted around April 22nd. I use an improved variety. Cotton is labor-intensive — my wife and I do the picking ourselves over three rounds in September and October. I can't afford to hire pickers at 80–100 yuan per day. The main problem is bollworms, so I spray insecticide three or four times. I also put down herbicide. Fertilizer is about 12 kg N per mu, split at planting and flowering, plus some phosphorus and potassium. I irrigate twice — at flowering and at boll stage. I'm expecting about 220 kg per mu of seed cotton.

The mungbean and red bean plots are tiny, 0.5 mu each. I plant them in mid-June. They don't need much — a small bag of compound fertilizer each, water once or twice, and family labor for harvesting. We eat most of it, but mungbean prices were good last year. I expect about 80 kg/mu from the mungbean and 70 kg/mu from the red bean.

All in all, seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, pesticide, and hired machinery will cost me about 3,200 yuan this year. That's a big chunk of our cash. I thought about cutting back on fertilizer to save money, but 2019 taught me that false economy costs more at harvest. I'd rather tighten our belt at home than risk a bad crop.
